script: セイバールート三日目-05
title: セイバールート三日目-05

pages.ja:
外に出た途端、肩に圧し掛かっていた重圧が消え去った。
あの神父から離れた、という事もあるが、
遠くからでも目立つ制服の遠坂と、
雨合羽を着込んだ金髪の少女が立っている、なんて光景が妙に味があって気が抜けたらしい。

pages.en:
The moment I step outside, the weight bearing down on my shoulders disappears.

Part of it is simply being away from that priest.

But the sight of Tohsaka standing there in her unmistakable school uniform beside a blond girl bundled in a rain cape has such a strange charm to it that I cannot help relaxing.
pages.mirrorMoon:
As soon as I leave, the pressure on my shoulders lifts.
Certainly, you could say that getting away from that priest helped.
But Tohsaka standing out in her uniform…
…And the blond-haired girl in a raincoat standing near her make a strangely well-matched sight that somehow takes the pressure off me.

」
セイバーは相変わらず無言だ。
じっとこっちを見ているあたり、俺がどんな選択をしたのか気になっているようだ。

pages.en:
“—”

Saber remains silent as ever.

The way she watches me without looking away suggests she wants to know what choice I made.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“”

She’s looking at me, so it seems she is interested in the decision I made.

pages.ja:
「行きましょう。町に戻るまでは一緒でしょ、わたしたち」
さっさと歩き出す遠坂。
それに続いて、俺たちも教会を後にした。

pages.en:
“Let's go. We're traveling together until we're back in town, aren't we?”

Tohsaka strides off without waiting.

We follow her and leave the church behind.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Let’s go. We’re going the same way until we get back to town.”
Tohsaka starts walking.
Following after her, we leave the church as well.

pages.ja:
三人で坂を下りていく。
来た時もそう話した方じゃないが、帰りは一段と会話がない。
その理由ぐらい、鈍感な俺でも分かっていた。
教会での一件で、俺は本当にマスターになったのだ。
遠坂が俺とセイバーから離れて歩いているのは、きっとそういう理由だろう。

pages.en:
The three of us walk down the hill.

We were hardly talkative on the way here, but the return journey is quieter still.

Even someone as oblivious as me understands why.

What happened inside the church has made me a Master in truth.

That must be why Tohsaka keeps her distance from Saber and me.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The three of us descend the hill together.
We didn’t talk much on the way here, but there’s even less talk now.
Even dull as I am, I know why.
After what happened at the church, I truly became a Master.
And that must be the reason Tohsaka is walking a little apart from us.

理解しているけど、そんなふうに遠坂を区別するのは嫌だった。

「え……？」
「あ、うん。アーチャーなら無事よ。……ま、セイバーにやられたダメージは簡単に消えそうにないから、しばらく実体化はさせられないだろうけど」
「じゃあ側にはいないのか」

pages.en:
“Tohsaka. Is your Servant all right?”

“Huh…?”

“Oh. Yes, Archer's safe. …The damage Saber did isn't going away anytime soon, though, so I doubt I'll be able to let him materialize for a while.”

“Then he isn't here with you?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Tohsaka. Is your Servant okay?”
“Huh…?”
“Oh yeah. Archer is okay. …Though it doesn’t seem like the damage caused by Saber will heal fast, so I don’t think I’ll be able to materialize him for a while.”
“Then he’s not with you right now?”

pages.ja: 「ええ、わたしの家で匿ってる状態。いま他のサーヴァントに襲われたら不利だから、傷が治るまでは有利な場所で敵に備えさせてるの」

pages.mirrorMoon: “No, he’s taking shelter at my house right now. He’ll be at a disadvantage if he was attacked by other Servants right now, so I’m making him stay ready at a place of strength.”

なるほど。
うちはともかく、遠坂の家なら敵に対する備えは万全なんだろう。

pages.en:
That makes sense.

I cannot speak for my place, but Tohsaka's home must be thoroughly fortified against attack.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I see.
Unlike my house, I’ll bet Tohsaka’s house is well prepared against attacks.

pages.ja:
魔術師にとって自分の家は要塞のような物だ。そこにいる限り、まず負ける事などない。
逆を言えば、ホームグランドにいる限り、敵は簡単には襲いかかってこないという事か。
……うむ。
うちの結界は侵入者に対する警報だけだが、それだけでも有ると無いとでは大違いだし。

pages.en:
To a mage, their home is a fortress. So long as they remain inside it, defeat is all but impossible.

Conversely, that must mean enemies will hesitate to attack while you are on your own ground.

…Right.

The bounded field around my house does nothing but warn me of intruders, yet even that makes a world of difference.
pages.mirrorMoon:
A house is like a fortress for a magus. They will not lose as long as they stay there.
That must mean enemies will not attack you as long as you stay on your home ground.
…I see.
The boundary field at my house is merely an alarm against intruders, but even having that makes a big difference.

pages.ja:
「そういえば遠坂。さっきヤツ、聖杯戦争の監督役って言ってたけどさ。アイツ、おまえのサーヴァントを知ってるのか」
「知らない筈よ。わたし、教えてないもの」
pages.jaRuby:
「そういえば遠坂。さっきヤツ、聖杯戦争の監督役って言ってたけどさ。アイツ、おまえのサーヴァントを知ってるのか」
「知らない筈よ。わたし、教えてないもの」
pages.en:
“Come to think of it, Tohsaka. That man said he was overseeing the Holy Grail War. Does he know who your Servant is?”

“He shouldn't. I never told him.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Oh yeah, Tohsaka. That guy said he was the supervisor of the Holy Grail War, but does he know your Servant?”
“He shouldn’t. I haven’t told him.”

pages.ja:
「そうなのか。おまえとアイツ、仲がいいからそうだと思ってたけど」
「……あのね衛宮くん。忠告しておくけど、自分のサーヴァントの正体は誰にも教えちゃ駄目よ。たとえ信用できる相手でも黙っておきなさい。そうでないと早々に消える事になるから」

pages.en:
“Really? You and he seem close, so I assumed he would.”

“…Listen, Emiya. Here's a word of advice: never tell anyone your Servant's identity. Keep it to yourself even around someone you trust. Otherwise, you and your Servant won't last long.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I see. You guys seem to have a good relationship, so I thought so.”
“…Hey Emiya-kun. I’ll warn you now. Don’t tell anybody your Servant’s identity. Keep it a secret even from people you trust or you’ll end up exiting this battle early.”

pages.ja:
「……？ セイバーの正体って、なにさ」
「だから、サーヴァントが何処の英雄かっていう事よ。
いくら強いからって戦力を明かしてちゃ、いつか寝首をかかれるに決まってるでしょ。……いいから、後でセイバーから真名を教えてもらいなさい。
そうすればわたしの言ってる事が判る……けど、ちょっとたんま。衛宮くんはアレだから、いっそ教えてもらわない方がいいわね」

pages.en:
“…? What do you mean, Saber's identity?”

“I mean which hero your Servant actually is.

“It doesn't matter how powerful you are. Reveal the forces at your disposal, and sooner or later someone will catch you in your sleep. …Just ask Saber for her True Name later.

“Then you'll understand what I'm talking about… Wait. You're *you*, Emiya. Maybe you'd be better off not knowing at all.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…? What do you mean Saber’s identity?”
“What I mean is, which hero the Servant is.
No matter how strong someone may be, if you reveal your potential, you’ll surely be beaten someday. …It’s fine, so have Saber tell you her real name later on.
You should understand what I mean then. …Though, hang on. You’re like this, so it might be better if she didn’t tell you.”

pages.ja:
「なんでさ」
「衛宮くん、隠し事できないもの。なら知らない方が秘密にできるじゃない」
「……あのな、人をなんだと思ってるんだ。それぐらいの駆け引きはできるぞ、俺」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“Why not?”

“Because you can't keep a secret. It's easier to conceal something you don't know.”

“…Hey, what kind of person do you think I am? I can manage that much subterfuge.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Why?”
“Because you can’t keep secrets. You’ll be able to keep a secret better if you don’t know about it.”
“…Hey now, what do you think I am? I can take care of myself.”

pages.ja:
「そう？ じゃあわたしに隠している事とかある？」
「え……遠坂に隠してる事って、それは」
口にして、ぼっと顔が熱くなった。
別に後ろめたい事なんてないけど、なんとなく憧れていた、なんて事は隠し事に入るんだろうか……？
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“Can you? Then are you hiding anything from me right now?”

“Huh…? Something I'm hiding from you? That would be—”

Heat rushes into my face as soon as I say it.

It is not as though I have anything to feel guilty about, but does the fact that I have always admired her from a distance count as a secret…?
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Really? Then do you have anything you’re hiding from me?”
“Huh…? Anything I’m hiding from you, that’s…”
I say, as my face fires up.
I don’t have a guilty conscience, but
well,
would kind of admiring her count as something I’m hiding from her…?

pages.ja:
「ほら見なさい。何を隠してるか知らないけど、動揺が顔に出るようじゃ向いてないわ。
貴方は他にいいところがあるんだから、駆け引きなんて考えるのは止めなさい」
pages.jaRuby:
「ほら見なさい。何を隠してるか知らないけど、動揺が顔に出るようじゃ向いてないわ。
貴方は他にいいところがあるんだから、駆け引きなんて考えるのは止めなさい」
pages.en:
“See? I don't know what you're hiding, but if every flicker of agitation shows on your face, you aren't cut out for this.

“You have other virtues. Stop imagining you can play games with people.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“See. I don’t know what you’re hiding, but it’s no good if it shows on your face.
You have other good aspects, so don’t worry about it.”

pages.ja: 「……む。それじゃ遠坂はどうなんだよ。あの神父にも黙ってるって事は、アイツも信用してないって事か？」
pages.jaRuby: 「……む。それじゃ遠坂はどうなんだよ。あの神父にも黙ってるって事は、アイツも信用してないって事か？」
pages.en: “…Hmph. Then what about you, Tohsaka? If you keep secrets from that priest too, does that mean you don't trust him?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “…Hmph. Then what about you? If you’re hiding it from that priest, does that mean you don’t trust him?”

pages.ja: 「綺礼？ まさか。私、アイツを信用するほどおめでたくないわ。アイツはね、教会から魔術協会に鞍替えしたくせに、まだ教会に在籍している食わせ者なのよ。人の情報を他のマスターに売るぐらいはやりかねないわ」

pages.en: “Kirei? As if. I'm not naive enough to trust *him*. He's a slippery bastard who switched allegiance from the Church to the Mage's Association and somehow still holds a position in the Church. Selling information about me to another Master wouldn't be beneath him.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Kirei? Hardly. I’m not crazy enough to trust him. He’s a cheat who transferred from the Church to the Magic Association without quitting the Church. He’d happily sell my information to the other Masters.”

pages.ja:
ふんだ、と忌々しげに言い捨てる遠坂。
遠坂は本気であの神父を信用してないようだ。
それはそれでホッとしたけど、それでも、なんとなく今の台詞には、神父への親しみが含まれている気がした。

pages.en:
Tohsaka spits the words out with a resentful snort.

She truly does not trust that priest.

That is reassuring in its own way. Even so, I cannot help feeling that her words held a certain familiarity toward him.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…Tohsaka says with annoyance.
It seems she really doesn’t trust that priest.
I’m a bit relieved, but still, her words do seem to hold a bit of affection.

pages.ja:
そうして橋を渡る。
もうお互いに会話はない。
冷たい冬の空気と、吐きだされる白い吐息。
水の流れる小さな音と、橋を照らす目映い街灯。
そういった様々なものが、今はひどく記憶に残る。

pages.en:
—And so we cross the bridge.

There is no conversation between us now.

The cold winter air. The white clouds of our breath.

The faint murmur of flowing water and the brilliant streetlamps shining over the bridge.

For some reason, every little thing sears itself into my memory.
pages.mirrorMoon:
And we pass the bridge.
There’s no conversation between us now.
The cold winter air and our cold breath.
A faint sound of flowing water and the white streetlamps that light up the bridge.
Small things like that are engraved into my memory.

pages.ja:
不思議と、遠坂の顔を見ようと思わなかった。
今は遠坂の顔を見るより、こうして一緒に歩いている事の方が得難いと思う。
俺と、遠坂と、まだ何も知らないセイバーという少女。
この三人で、何をするでもなく、帰るべき場所へと歩いていく。

pages.en:
Strangely, I feel no urge to look at Tohsaka's face.

Right now, simply walking beside her seems more precious than seeing her expression.

Me, Tohsaka, and Saber, the girl I still know nothing about.

The three of us walk together toward the places where we belong, with no purpose beyond going home.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Oddly, I didn’t think about looking at
Tohsaka.
Tohsaka, who’s walking next to me.
Right now, it seems walking
on a bridge at night
together like this is more precious than seeing her face.
Me, Tohsaka, and the girl called Saber I know nothing about.
We three walk together without doing much.

pages.ja:
交差点に着いた。
それぞれの家に続く坂道の交差点、衛宮士郎と遠坂凛が別れる場所。
pages.jaRuby:
交差点に着いた。
それぞれの家に続く坂道の交差点、衛宮士郎と遠坂凛が別れる場所。
pages.en:
We reach the intersection.

Here the hills leading to our respective homes diverge. Here Shirou Emiya and Rin Tohsaka part ways.
pages.mirrorMoon:
We reach the intersection.
The intersection that leads to our houses, the place where we must part with Tohsaka.

pages.ja:
「ここでお別れね。義理は果たしたし、これ以上一緒にいると何かと面倒でしょ。きっぱり別れて、明日からは敵同士にならないと」
今までの曖昧な位置づけに区切りをつける為だろう。
遠坂は何の前置きもなく喋りだして、唐突に話を切った。
pages.jaRuby:
「ここでお別れね。義理は果たしたし、これ以上一緒にいると何かと面倒でしょ。きっぱり別れて、明日からは敵同士にならないと」

pages.en:
“This is where we say goodbye. I've discharged my obligation, and staying together any longer will only complicate things. We need to make a clean break so we can be enemies starting tomorrow.”

Perhaps she means to draw a line beneath the ambiguity between us until now.

Without preamble, Tohsaka begins to speak—and brings the matter to an equally abrupt end.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“We’ll part here. I’ve repaid my debt, and it would be troublesome if we stayed together any longer. We should part and become enemies from tomorrow on.”
It must be to end the ambiguous position we are in right now.
Tohsaka starts talking and cuts off suddenly.

pages.ja:
それで分かった。
彼女は義務感から俺にルールを説明したんじゃない。
あくまで公平に、何も知らない衛宮士郎の立場になって肩入れしただけなのだ。
だから説明さえ終われば元通り。
あとはマスターとして、争うだけの対象になる。
pages.jaRuby:
それで分かった。
彼女は義務感から俺にルールを説明したんじゃない。
あくまで公平に、何も知らない衛宮士郎の立場になって肩入れしただけなのだ。
だから説明さえ終われば元通り。
あとはマスターとして、争うだけの対象になる。
pages.en:
That is when I understand.

She did not explain the rules out of some dry sense of obligation.

She simply put herself in the place of Shirou Emiya, who knew nothing, and chose to help him in the name of fairness.

Now that her explanation is over, things return to the way they were.

From here on, I am only someone she must fight as a fellow Master.
pages.mirrorMoon:
From that, I realize.
She did not explain the rules to me out of any sense of obligation.
She just supported me, understanding the situation I’m in, and acted fairly.
So things are back to normal once the explanations are over.
I will just be her target as a Master now.

けど、だとしたら今のはヘンだろう。
遠坂は感情移入をすると戦いにくくなる、と言いたかったに違いない。
遠坂から見れば今夜の事は全て余分。
“これ以上一緒にいると何かと面倒”
そんな台詞を口にするのなら、遠坂は初めから一緒にいなければ良かったのだ。

pages.en:
“…Hm?”

But in that case, what she just said makes no sense.

She must have meant that growing attached would make it harder to fight.

From her perspective, everything she did tonight was unnecessary.

*Staying together any longer will only complicate things.*

If she was going to say that, then she should never have accompanied me in the first place.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Hm?”
But if so, what she just said was strange.
Tohsaka must have meant that it would be difficult to fight if she feels empathy for me.
For Tohsaka, everything that happened tonight must have been unnecessary.
‘It would be troublesome if we stay together any longer.’
If she is going to say something like that, she should have left us alone from the beginning.

聡明な遠坂の事だから、それは判りきっている筈。
それでも損得勘定を秤にもかけないで、遠坂凛は衛宮士郎の手を取った。

Tohsaka is clever. She must have known that perfectly well.

Yet Rin Tohsaka took Shirou Emiya's hand without once weighing profit against loss.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Tohsaka’s smart, so she should know that all too well.
But still, she set aside all thought of loss or gain and helped me out.

pages.ja:
だから今夜の件は何の思惑もない、本当にただの善意。
目の前にいる遠坂は、学校で見る彼女とはあまりにも違う。
控えめにいっても性格はきついし、ツンケンしていて近寄りがたいし、学校での振る舞いはなんなんだー、と言いたくなるぐらいの変わり様だ。

pages.en:
So there was no ulterior motive behind tonight. It was an act of genuine kindness.

The Tohsaka before me could hardly be more different from the girl I see at school.

Even putting it mildly, she is sharp-tongued, prickly, and difficult to approach. The contrast is so dramatic I want to demand what all that immaculate behavior at school is supposed to be.
pages.mirrorMoon:
So what happened tonight was totally out of good faith.
The Tohsaka in front of me is too different from how she is at school.
Even when I put it nicely, she’s sour, cranky, unapproachable, and she’s so different that I want to scream out.

pages.ja:
いやもう、こんなのほとんどサギだと思う。
……だが、まあそれでも。
遠坂凛は、みんなが思っていた通りの彼女でもあったのだ。
pages.jaRuby:
いやもう、こんなのほとんどサギだと思う。

遠坂凛は、みんなが思っていた通りの彼女でもあったのだ。
pages.en:
Honestly, it borders on fraud.

…But even so.

Rin Tohsaka is also exactly the person everyone believed her to be.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Man, it feels almost like a fraud.
…Yet, still…
Tohsaka Rin is just how everyone thought she was.

「なんだ。遠坂っていいヤツなんだな」
「は？ なによ突然。おだてたって手は抜かないわよ」
そんな事は判ってる。
コイツは手を抜かないからこそ、情が移ると面倒だって言い切ったんだから。

“Huh. You're a good person, Tohsaka.”

“What? Where did that come from? Flattery isn't going to make me hold back.”

I know that.

It is precisely because she will not hold back that she said becoming attached would be a problem.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I see. Tohsaka, you really are a good person.”
“Huh? What are you saying all of a sudden? I won’t go easy on you even if you flatter me.”
I know that.
She won’t go easy on me, and that’s why she said it’ll be a bother if she feels empathy for me.

“I'd rather not owe that place anything, but I'll keep it in mind. I doubt it'll come to that, though. However you look at it, I'm the one with the shorter life expectancy, not Saber.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“A-Anyway, just run to the church if your Servant ever gets killed. If you do, at least your life will be safe.”
“I won’t like it, but still, I’ll take that advice. It won’t happen, though. However I look at it, I’ll die before Saber does.”

「
ふう」

彼女は呆れた風に溜息をこぼした後、ちらり、とセイバーを流し見た。

I give her an objective assessment of the situation.

“—Honestly.”

Tohsaka responds with yet another reaction I cannot decipher.

She lets out an exasperated sigh, then flicks a sidelong glance at Saber.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I calmly analyze the situation.
“Phew.”
Tohsaka reacts strangely once again.
After letting out a sigh, she glances at Saber.

せいぜい気を付けなさい。いくらセイバーが優れているからって、マスターである貴方がやられちゃったらそれまでなんだから」

pages.en:
“Fine. Any more advice really *would* mean I'm getting attached, so I won't say another word.

“Just be careful. Saber may be exceptional, but if her Master gets himself killed, it's over for both of you.”

Tohsaka turns on her heel and begins to walk away.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“All right. I won’t give you any more warnings because that’d really be empathy.
Just be careful. Even though Saber is strong, it won’t matter if you, her Master, gets killed.”
She turns her back and starts walking.

her feet stop dead, as abruptly as though she has seen a ghost.

The moment I call her name, a sharp pain stabs through my left hand.

視線が坂の上に引き寄せられる。
いつのまに雲は去ったのか、空には煌々と輝く月。
そこには。

A child's voice rings through the night.

The lilting sound unmistakably belongs to a young girl.

My gaze is drawn to the top of the hill.

At some point the clouds have parted, leaving the moon to blaze in the sky.

—And there—

The voice like a song is unmistakably that of a young girl.
My vision is drawn to the top of the hill.
I don’t know when the clouds parted, but a bright moon is now shining in the sky.
There.

A shadow stretches across the ground.

In the dim blue silhouette of the town stands something misshapen that has no right to exist.
pages.mirrorMoon:
A long shadow.
There’s a strange shape that shouldn’t be here in this pale town of shadow pictures.

Her innocence sends a chill down my spine.

The girl smiles as she says so.

All fears and impatience are drowned by hopelessness, so I don’t feel a thing.

「
やば。あいつ、桁違いだ」
麻痺している俺とは違い、遠坂には身構えるだけの余裕がある。
……しかし、それも僅かな物だろう。
背中越しだというのに、彼女が抱いている絶望を感じ取れるんだから。

坂の上、俺たちを見下ろしながら、少女は不満そうに言う。
……ますますやばい。
あの少女には、遠坂のサーヴァントが不在だという事も見抜かれている。
と。
少女は行儀良く、この場に不釣り合いなお辞儀をした。
「はじめまして、リン。わたしはイリヤ。
イリヤスフィール・フォン・アインツベルンって言えばわかるでしょ？」

」
その名前に聞き覚えでもあるのか、遠坂の体がかすかに揺れた。

「じゃあいくね。やっちゃえ、バーサーカー」

巨体が飛ぶ。

！
「
シロウ、下がって……！」

バーサーカーの落下地点まで駆けるセイバーと、
旋風を伴って落下してきたバーサーカーとは、まったくの同時だった。

ざざざざ、という音。
バーサーカーの大剣を受けたものの、セイバーは受け止めた剣ごと押し戻される。

セイバーの姿勢が崩れる。
追撃する鉛色のサーヴァント。
灰色の異形は、それしか知らぬかのように大剣を叩きつける。
避ける間もなく剣で受けるセイバー。
彼女の剣が見えなかろうと関係ない。
バーサーカーの一撃は全身で受け止めなければ防ぎきれない即死の風だ。
故に、セイバーは受けに回るしかない。
彼女にとって、勝機とはバーサーカーの剣戟の合間に活路を見いだす事。
だが。
それも、バーサーカーに隙があればの話。
黒い岩盤の剣は、それこそ嵐のようだった。
あれほどの巨体。
あれほどの大剣を以ってして、バーサーカーの速度はセイバーを上回っている。
繰り出される剣戟は、ただ叩きつけるだけの、何の工夫もない駄剣だ。

圧倒的なまでの力と速度が有るのなら、技の介入する余地などない。
技巧とは、人間が欠点を補うために編み出すもの。
そんな弱点、あの巨獣には存在しない。

凍り付いた体で、ただ、そう呟いた。
アレには勝てない。

絶え間なく繰り出される死の嵐。
捌ききれず後退したセイバーに、今度こそ、
防ぎ切れぬ、終りの一撃が繰り出された。

pages.en:
“—This is bad. That thing is in another league.”

Unlike me, paralyzed where I stand, Tohsaka has enough composure left to take a fighting stance.

…But even that composure must be slight.

Her back is turned to me, yet I can still feel the despair inside her.

“Oh? Your Servant is taking a nap. That's no fun. I was going to crush both your pets together.”

The girl looks down on us from the top of the hill and pouts.

…This is getting worse.

She has seen through the fact that Tohsaka's Servant is absent.

—Then—

The girl gives a prim little bow grotesquely out of place in this scene.

“It's nice to meet you, Rin. I'm Illya.

“Illyasviel von Einzbern. That name should tell you who I am, shouldn't it?”

“Einzbern—”

Perhaps she recognizes the name. Tohsaka's body trembles faintly.

Pleased by her reaction, the girl breaks into a delighted smile.

“All right, here we go. Get them, Berserker.”

She sings the order to the monstrosity behind her.

The giant mass takes flight.

The thing she called Berserker drops from the top of the hill to where we stand—a distance of dozens of meters—in a single bound—!

“—Shirou, get back…!”

Saber runs. Her rain cape tears loose, blinding me for a single instant.

Saber reaches the point where Berserker will land at precisely the same instant that Berserker descends in a whirlwind.

“……!”

The air shudders.

Saber has caught Berserker's greatsword—a slab of stone in all but name—upon her invisible blade.

“—”

Saber's mouth twists with strain.

Then Berserker's greatsword flashes again like a cyclone—!

A thunderous crash.

Steel collides with steel hard enough to tear the air apart, and Saber loses the exchange.

A long, grinding scrape.

She catches Berserker's greatsword, but it drives her backward together with the blade she raised to block it.

“Kh…”

Saber's stance buckles.

The leaden Servant presses the attack.

The gray aberration brings down its greatsword as though that is the only act it knows.

Saber has no time to evade. She meets it with her blade.

It makes no difference that Berserker cannot see her weapon.

Each of his blows is a wind of instant death, impossible to stop unless she receives it with her entire body.

And so Saber can do nothing but defend.

Her only chance is to find a way through in the intervals between Berserker's strikes.

But that assumes Berserker leaves an opening.

The black stone blade is a storm unto itself.

For all his monstrous size, for all the weight of that enormous sword, Berserker is faster than Saber.

His attacks possess no ingenuity at all. They are crude swings that do nothing but smash downward.

Yet that is enough.

When power and speed are absolute, technique has no room to intervene.

Technique is something human beings devised to compensate for their flaws.

That great beast possesses no such weakness.

“—Run.”

With my body frozen, I can do no more than whisper the word.

She cannot defeat that thing.

If this continues, Saber will be killed.

She has to run.

Alone, she could escape easily.

She must understand that better than anyone…!

“Ah—”

This is bad.

My body may be numb, but my mind is working with perfect clarity.

The storm of death never lets up.

Saber has been forced backward, unable to turn aside every blow. And now—

the final strike comes, one she cannot possibly block.

“…!”

There,
Berserker’s gigantic sword flashes like a whirlwind!
A great thunderous roar.
The crash of steel that almost tears the air results in defeat for Saber.
A sliding sound.
Even though she blocked Berserker’s giant sword, she is driven back along with the sword she used to block it.
“Guh…”
Saber’s posture collapses.
The lead colored Servant chases after her.
The gray figure swings its giant sword as if it’s the only thing it knows how to do.
Saber doesn’t have the time to dodge it and blocks it with her sword.
It does not matter if Saber’s sword is invisible or not.
Each of Berserker’s attacks is a fatal one that must be blocked with all her might.
Therefore, Saber has to stay on the defense.
For her, the only chance of victory is to find a means of attack in between Berserker’s attacks.
But.
That’s only if Berserker leaves an opening.
The black rock sword is just like a storm.
With such a large body.
And with such a large sword, and yet Berserker is moving faster than Saber.
The attacks he sends out are just smashing swings with no technique to them.
But that’s enough.
If there is overwhelming power and speed, there is no room for technique.
Techniques are something humans invented to compensate for their weaknesses.
Weaknesses are things that giant doesn’t have.
“Run.”
I murmur with my frozen body.
That thing cannot be defeated.
Saber will be killed if we go on like this.
So she should run away.
It would be easy for her to get away if it were just her here.
She should know that already…!
“Oh”
That’s bad.
My body is numb, but maybe that’s why my mind is so calm.
The storm of death that strikes without a pause.
Unable to take all the attacks, Saber retreats, and this time…
The final blow that cannot be blocked is swung.

—She falls in a great arc.

Before her back can strike the ground, Saber twists in the air and lands on her feet.

“…Ngh…!”

Somehow, Saber regains her balance.

But red blood is spreading across her chest.

“—That's…”

…What an idiot I am.

I forgot something crucial.

I do not know how many battles a Servant can endure in one day, but this is already Saber's third.

And the wound Lancer drove through her chest is still there—

“N—gh—”

Saber braces herself as though shielding her chest.

Berserker descends on the wounded Saber like a hurricane—

and multiple bolts of force strike him in the back.

“—Fourfold fire…!”

Whatever the magecraft may be, Berserker's body erupts beneath Tohsaka's incantation.

Judging from the torrent of magical energy, each direct hit lands with something like the impact of a large-caliber handgun.

But even that is useless.

Not a single wound appears on Berserker's body.

He is not nullifying the magecraft as Saber does.

It simply has no effect on him at all.

“…!? Damn it, what kind of ridiculous body does this thing have…!?”

Still, Tohsaka does not let up.

Berserker ignores her magecraft and charges Saber.

“……”

Saber raises her head in pain.

She lifts her sword, still intent on fighting.

—And at that, my frozen body comes free.

pages.en:
“No! Run, Saber…!”

I shout with every scrap of strength I possess.

At the sound—

she turns to face an enemy she cannot possibly defeat.

Berserker's onslaught has no end.

Each blow drives Saber's body lower, bringing her closer by the second to the final moment.

—And yet, where can such strength reside in so small a body?

Saber does not yield a single step.

She catches every greatsword blow in the raging torrent and tries, through sheer force of will, to drive Berserker back.

There is no hope of victory.

She knows that continuing this battle means defeat, yet the sight of her holding her ground is somehow unnatural.

Whatever he sees in that sight—

the misshapen giant, silent until now, roars.

The next stroke cannot be defended against.

It scythes through Saber's perfect guard and sends her flying at last.

A heavy thud.

Something lands far away.

…Fresh blood scatters through the air.

And there, in a body that should never be able to rise again—

“Ah… ngh…”

she stands, unconscious.

As though, if she did not, I would be the one left behind to die.

“—”

And then—

I understand just how foolish a choice I have made.

Berserker stops after cutting Saber down.

He pays no attention to Tohsaka or me where we stand. He merely waits for his Master's command from the top of the hill.

“Ahaha. Of course you couldn't win. My Berserker is the greatest hero in all of Greece.”

“…!? The greatest hero in Greece—you can't mean—”

“That's right. The monster standing there is Heracles.

“He's the most terrible monster of them all, in an entirely different class from the heroes people like you could ever command.”
